deficiencies.description: The rewrite omits the causal link explaining why the muscularis mucosae is used as a proxy for the basement membrane (the lecturer states this is because it is the thin layer of musculature situated directly underneath the epithelium).

deficiencies.description: The rewrite omits the consideration of whether there are secondary metastases across the body following the identification of an invasive, likely malignant tumour.
deficiencies.sourcePassage: But the question is, of course, you would then be interested in figuring out whether or not there would be secondary metastases across the body.

considerations.sourcePassage: Right. So obviously, let me just orient you here. You're looking at, whoops, the normal colonic epithelium, which as you see, secretes a lot of mucus, so it's quite shiny and smooth. And then as you're looking along, you will see this giant cauliflower shaped structure here, which is obviously pathological.
considerations.reason: The conversational filler, orientation remarks, and presenter false starts ('let me just orient you here', 'whoops', 'as you see') were appropriately omitted as spoken commentary, while the visual descriptions of the epithelium and the pathological cauliflower-shaped structure were accurately preserved.

considerations.sourcePassage: Right. So, for the next slides that I'm going to look at, just imagine that you've sliced along the plane here, where the red line is, so you're looking through a slice of the head of the cauliflower, right?
considerations.reason: The rewrite converts the lecturer's direct address to the audience into passive academic prose ('the tissue is imagined as sliced along the plane marked by the red line') without adding ungrounded facts or changing the meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: And just to orient you here, you have normal and you have the muscle underneath.
considerations.reason: The lecturer says 'normal', which the rewrite renders as 'normal epithelium'. This is supported by the lecturer's subsequent mention of 'the normal epithelium here in green'.

considerations.sourcePassage: and then your normal musculature located here.
considerations.reason: The rewrite phrases this as 'located beneath', which is faithful to the lecturer's earlier statement that 'you have the muscle underneath'.

considerations.reason: The conversational reference to what was said previously ('remember I told you that') is dropped filler/remark to audience.

considerations.sourcePassage: So invasion and malignancy are really, really important diagnostically. So it's defined as the ability to invade the surrounding tissue.
considerations.reason: The singular pronoun 'it' was resolved to 'malignancy', which is the conventional definition in oncology (as defining 'invasion' as the ability to invade would be tautological).

considerations.sourcePassage: And in order to do that, as I said, we are studying these precursor stages, in their development into this more malignant state.
considerations.reason: Converting 'as I said, we are studying' to the passive voice 'the precursor stages are studied' removes conversational framing without altering the factual meaning.

considerations.sourcePassage: So those are all very, very good questions and very, very pertinent questions because, as I said, most of the death with cancer happens to be with the malignant tumors in the other organs, in the distant organs.
considerations.reason: Omitting 'very, very good questions and' and 'as I said' drops rhetorical repetition and lecture framing while preserving the core causal statement.
